title: Multi-metric fidelity harness and gating for FP8/INT8 quant profiles
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a robust, reproducible quality-metrics harness that evaluates FP8 and INT8 quantization profiles across a representative suite of tasks and implements automated gating rules for calibration pipelines. The harness will: 1) compute standard aggregate metrics (perplexity on language-model validation sets), 2) run MMLU-style multiple-choice suites and compute accuracy, 3) compute text-generation overlap metrics (ROUGE, BLEU) for summarization/MT workloads, and 4) provide task-specific scorers for extractive QA (EM/F1), NER (span-F1), and code/code-synthesis tests (exact-match, pass@k). The output will be a per-profile report (CSV + JSON) with FP32 baseline deltas, per-task confidence intervals, and a derived weighted-fidelity score used by the calibration CI gate.
acceptance_criteria: Harness runs end-to-end on CI for a profile sweep and produces per-profile report artifacts (CSV + JSON) stored in S3.
Perplexity computed on standard LM validation sets matches reference baseline within 1.5x variance bounds for repeated runs.
MMLU-suite accuracy computed and compared to FP32 baseline; gating rules flag any task with >3% absolute drop or >7% relative drop.
ROUGE/BLEU pipelines implemented for summarization and MT datasets with tokenization and length-penalty handling consistent with eval-harness canonical implementations.
Task-specific scorers (QA, NER, retrieval rerank) implemented as plugins and exercised in CI for one representative dataset each.
Derived weighted-fidelity score computed with per-task weights configurable from the project config; default weights set by PM/Research.
Harness integrates with existing calibration orchestration so that a failed gate prevents profile promotion to canary and triggers a rollback policy.
Dashboard (Console) ingest path documented so per-profile metrics appear under release/runtime-1.20 quantization tab.
End-to-end regression test included in the quant calibration pipeline with a badge showing pass/fail for the release branch.
Documentation (Confluence) and a short runbook for interpreting failures provided for SRE and Solutions Engineering teams.
risks: Metric noise for short evaluation runs: small sample sizes on rare tasks can produce volatile deltas.
Mismatch between tokenization and metric implementations (ROUGE/BLEU) producing inconsistent scores vs external benchmarks.
Compute cost for full suite is non-trivial; need to balance coverage vs CI runtime budgets.
Weighting scheme could bias selection toward tasks that are cheaper to evaluate if not audited by PM/Research.
Edge cases where quantized model produces valid but semantically different outputs that automated metrics penalize incorrectly.
design_decisions: Use FP32 run as baseline; every quant profile report contains absolute and relative delta columns against FP32.
Implement metric adapters as small Python entrypoints under eval-adapters/ with a consistent CLI so CI and local dev can invoke them identically.
Confidence intervals are computed with bootstrap resampling (default 1000 samples) to quantify metric stability.
Weighted-fidelity score computed as sum_i w_i * normalized_delta_i where normalization uses robust scaling (median, IQR) to reduce sensitivity to outliers.
Default gating rule: weighted-fidelity >= 0.95 AND no single task with absolute drop > 3% OR relative drop > 7%.
Keep metric implementations dependency-light and vendor-agnostic; reuse existing eval-harness code where possible but avoid deep coupling to avoid maintenance burden.
implementation_notes: Initial PR created that adds scaffold for perplexity, MMLU adapter, and rouge adapter. See GH PR link in attachments.
Added tokenizer normalization utility to ensure consistent detokenization across tasks; will be upstreamed to eval-harness common utils.
Caching policy: allow incremental evaluation. CI will run a fast smoke suite (subset of tasks) and nightly runs will run the full suite for stability reports.
Outputs: per-run artifact directory schema /s3/quant-reports/{profile}/{run_ts}/{artifacts} with report.json, metrics.csv, raw-predictions.jsonl.
We will sample 10k examples for perplexity-related tests and smaller canonical splits for RL/MMLU/QA tasks to keep compute bounded.
